messages.subject: epc interpretation
parts:
Does the epc in the modindices() output lead to a definite result when you free those parameters in the new model? 
I tried doing it, but it leads to different estimates. 


model <- 'visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3;
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6;
speed = ~ x7 + x8+ + x9'

fit<- cfa(model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit, standardized = TRUE, fit.measures=TRUE)

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: epc interpretation
parts: The M.I. and EPC statistic assume that no other parameter estimates will change value when the one constraint is removed. If you fixed all current parameter estimates at their current values but removed the one constraint, M.I. and EPC would hit the mark, pretty much exactly. M.I. is a derivative of the one constraint only, not a multivariate derivative.
